notes:
Both paper titles verified independently. No full original or replication paper acquired through permitted routes. Abstracts and secondary descriptions were not used for statistical extraction or an authors’ target-specific replication verdict. Acquisition details recorded in the two DOI-keyed .miss files in texts/.
Source follow-up: Original-only blind validation. Source is the published six-page article, printed pp. 1169–1174, rather than a manuscript or supplement. Title and authors visually verified on PDF p. 1. Rendered PDF p. 3 was inspected: the statistic is partial eta-squared .08 and p < .05. Frozen canonical text renders equals signs as 5 and ηp² as Zp 2; quotations preserve those exact OCR glyphs. The analytic sample inferred from the explicitly stated recruitment and exclusion is 50; the printed F denominator df is 49, which is inconsistent with an ordinary two-group ANOVA on 50 participants. Retained the printed F unchanged and did not infer sample size from its df. The mood-adjusted p = .095 is a different test and is not combined with this effect size. Supplied locator p. 4 is displaced: the matching Study 2 target is on printed p. 1171 / PDF p. 3; PDF p. 4 contains Studies 3 and 4.
Source follow-up: 2015 SSRN author manuscript retained as supplied. Study_r=3 is not a manuscript study label; outcome and p.9 locator uniquely identify the confirmatory full-sample test.
Completion source review (es_value_o): The explicitly identified Study 2 voice/importance outcome has printed partial eta squared .08 for the unadjusted heavy-versus-light one-way ANOVA. PDF inspection confirms metric identity despite canonical text OCR. The printed metric is partial eta squared; locator pagination is discrepant but study and outcome match.
